**EWS rules engine (parallel track):** Out-of-band 5-commit series shipped 2026-05-06 from a separate brief — a dedicated EWS-specific rules surface beside the existing M5 platform-static template library. Lives at `/v1/ews/rules/*` with 9 routes (CRUD + lifecycle + ad-hoc test + bulk evaluate + execution telemetry); 15-indicator EWS catalog spanning 10 domains (credit, insurance, fraud, kyc, transaction, agent, operational, portfolio, behaviour, risk_score) disjoint from regulatory-svc/BIL by EWS- ID prefix; pure executor with cumulative weighted scoring (sum/cap-100/RED≥75-ORANGE≥50-YELLOW≥25-GREEN); 1000-rule perf budget verified at the HTTP route layer (<500 ms); audit-event + M9.4 case-event side-effects on every match; 10 brief-mandated default rules + DB migration + SQL seed (forward-looking schema, runtime in-memory); SPA visual builder at `/rules/ews`. **EWS Rules-Plus extensions (RP-1..3, parallel track):** 3-commit follow-on shipped 2026-05-06 against the 8-task Hinglish brief (Add / Edit / Delete / Clone / Maker-Checker / 15 APIs / 3 DB tables / UI). Strictly additive on top of the base rules engine — base routes + state machine untouched. **RP-1** ships SemVer versions per rule (`bumpSemver` + `classifyEditBump`; cap 50/rule FIFO), 4-eyes maker-checker (`/submit` + `/approve` + `/reject` with self-approval refused at app **and** DB CHECK constraint), `/clone` (DRAFT v0.1.0; works on DEPRECATED rules), `/versions` list/detail, structured `/versions/diff` (field-by-field with kind: changed/added/removed), `/approvals` audit trail; 2 new DB tables (`app.ews_rule_versions`, `app.ews_rule_approvals`) in `015_ews_rules_versions.sql`; 51 new tests. **RP-2** ships SPA — 4-step modal wizard at `/rules/ews/wizard` (Basic Info → Conditions → Action → Lifecycle), auto-save 30s to localStorage, keyboard shortcuts (Cmd+S save-or-submit · Esc cancel · Cmd+Enter advance), inline pure-client Test Rule preview, side-by-side colored diff viewer (rose-50 before / emerald-50 after), per-row Clone modal; 14 new tests. **RP-3** ships docs — operator README + Postman walkthrough (12 requests covering 4-eyes flow + version snapshots + diff + clone + reject path) + 8-task checklist mapping. Architecture: `docs/ews-rules-plus-mapping.md`. README: `docs/ews-rules-plus-readme.md`. Production `vite build` resolved cleanly (aurora.line IS in tailwind.config.ts), but Tailwind 3 JIT's `@apply` lookup for **nested-theme colors** races in the vite dev pipeline → "The `border-aurora-line` class does not exist" at runtime, blanking the entire SPA on the user's localhost ("na to dashboard dikh rha h na hi koi modules"). **Root cause: production `vite build` alone wasn't sufficient verification for an `@apply`-on-nested-theme-color change.** Fix: kept `@apply bg-white border rounded-[14px]` for width + radius + bg, but inlined `border-color: #E4E7F2` (same hex bound to `theme.colors.aurora.line`) — no Tailwind class lookup for the border at all → racer eliminated. Case-insensitive + whitespace-trimmed. Malformed last_run_at → unparseable_schedule (defensive). ### 2026-05-21 — T3.1.1 — CBS production resilience framework (Phase 2a)

- [agent-integration] T3.1.1 shipped — production resilience layer over the existing CBS sync surface (cbs_sync.ts already shipped the ledger + reconciliation + monitoring; T3.1.1 layers retry / circuit breaker / audit-trail wrapping). New module `services/bff/src/integrations/cbs_production.ts`: **`CbsClient` interface** — minimal `call(req: CbsRequest) → Promise<CbsResponse<T>>` contract any concrete impl satisfies (HTTP REST / SOAP gateway / file drop / test stub). **`CbsRequest`** carries `operation`, optional `idempotency_key`, opaque `payload`; **`CbsResponse<T>`** has `ok / status / body / pending?` (pending=true for async-processed CBS operations the caller polls). **Retry policy** — `RetryPolicy` exposes `max_attempts / initial_backoff_ms / max_backoff_ms / jitter / retryable_statuses / non_retryable_operations?`. `DEFAULT_CBS_RETRY_POLICY` = 4 attempts, 250ms→8000ms exponential, ±20% jitter, retryable on {429, 500, 502, 503, 504}. Pure `computeBackoffMs(attempt, policy, randomFn)` exposed for tests with the jitter formula documented inline. **Circuit breaker** — `CircuitBreaker` class with 3 states (closed → open → half_open → closed) parameterised by `failure_threshold` / `recovery_timeout_ms` / `half_open_success_threshold`. `DEFAULT_CIRCUIT_BREAKER` = 5 failures trip / 30s recovery / 2 successes to close. Defensive: any failure in half_open re-opens immediately; success in closed resets the consecutive counter; `currentState()` recomputes open→half_open lazily when the recovery window has elapsed (no background timer needed). Deterministic `clock` injection for tests. **`CbsAuditSink`** interface — pluggable so production wires the M15.1 AuditTrailStore without forcing a hard import dependency on cbs_production.ts. `NoopCbsAuditSink` for tests. Audit records carry `tenant_id / actor_username / action: 'cbs.call.<operation>' / outcome: success|failure|denied / severity: info|warning|critical / metadata` (attempts, status, idempotency_key, error, non_retryable, reason). **`ResilientCbsClient`** decorator class wraps any inner `CbsClient` with the production patterns. `dispatch(req, tenant_id)` flow: (1) reject empty tenant_id; (2) check circuit — if open, audit `denied:circuit_open` + throw `CbsCircuitOpenError`; (3) loop up to `max_attempts`: call inner, on `ok: true` record success + return `DispatchOutcome`, on non-retryable failure (status not in `retryable_statuses` OR `operation` in `non_retryable_operations`) record failure + throw `CbsRetryExhaustedError`, on retryable failure compute backoff via `computeBackoffMs` + sleep + retry, on network exception throw if last attempt else retry; (4) on exhaustion record failure + throw. **DispatchOutcome** returns `response + attempts + total_latency_ms + circuit_state` for ops observability. **2 error types**: `CbsCircuitOpenError` (carries `operation`); `CbsRetryExhaustedError` (carries `operation + attempts + lastStatus + cause`). Deterministic test injection via `clock` / `randomFn` / `sleepMs` options. 18 new jest tests cover: `computeBackoffMs` doubling per attempt + max clamp + jitter band; CircuitBreaker state machine (closed → open at threshold; open → half_open after timeout; half_open → closed after success threshold; half_open → open on any failure; closed success resets counter); ResilientCbsClient happy path + retry on 503 + retry exhaustion + non-retryable 400 + non_retryable_operations enforcement + circuit OPEN rejects + persistent failures trip the breaker + network exception retries + empty tenant_id rejected + NoopCbsAuditSink callable. All 18/18 pass. tsc clean. **Closes T3.1 in code** — production CBS adapters wrap their concrete impl with `new ResilientCbsClient(httpCbsClient, {audit, retryPolicy, circuit})` and get retry + breaker + audit automatically. The existing M14 `InsuranceAdapter` / `Ifrs9Adapter` / `AmlAdapter` / `DmsAdapter` / `BureauAdapter` / `AgentAdapter` / `FinanceAdapter` / `HrAdapter` interfaces can adopt the same pattern in follow-up tickets. **What's deployed:** code + tests. **What remains for Year-2:** wire a real HTTP `CbsClient` impl pointing at the bank's CBS API; configure the audit sink to call the M15.1 AuditTrailStore; tune `RetryPolicy` + `CircuitBreaker` thresholds from the first 30 days of production traffic.

### 2026-05-21 — T5.1.1 — Retraining schedule + outcome ledger

- [agent-ai + agent-integration] T5.1.1 shipped — closes the "no training scheduler is wired" gap of T5.1 (the auto-promotion gate from 2026-05-09 has been waiting for this counterpart). The full continuous-learning loop is now operable: **schedule → external trainer fires → POST outcome → fleet status view → auto-promotion gate decision**. The actual model training (`ml/pipelines/train_pd.py`) stays external — when it finishes, an external scheduler (Airflow / manual / future cron) POSTs the outcome to the BFF ledger and ops gets a fleet-wide "are we current on retraining?" view without coupling the BFF to Python execution. New module `services/bff/src/ai_retraining.ts`: **5 cadence values** in canonical order — `monthly / quarterly / biannual / annual / drift_triggered` (the last carries an optional `drift_trigger_threshold` 0..1 representing PSI/KS above which a retrain is required; time-based cadences derive `next_retrain_at` via `computeNextRetrainAt`). **4 outcome statuses** — `success / failure / rolled_back / in_progress`. **`computeNextRetrainAt(cadence, anchor)`** pure helper adds 1/3/6/12 UTC months for monthly/quarterly/biannual/annual; `drift_triggered` returns null (no scheduled time — retrain fired on drift event from the agent-ai drift monitor). **3 type guards** (`isRetrainingCadence`, `isRetrainingOutcomeStatus`) + closed-enum exports `ALL_RETRAINING_CADENCES` + `ALL_RETRAINING_OUTCOME_STATUSES`. **`RetrainingScheduleEntry`** carries schedule_id (`rts-<tenant>-<ts>-<seq>`) + tenant_id + model_id + cadence + next_retrain_at + last_retrained_at (null initially) + drift_trigger_threshold + enabled + notes + created_at/by + updated_at. **`RetrainingOutcome`** carries outcome_id (`rto-<tenant>-<ts>-<seq>`) + schedule_id (nullable — ad-hoc training tied to no schedule allowed) + model_id + status + started_at/completed_at + duration_ms (computed) + new_version + metrics (flat number Record — typically `{auc, brier, ks, n_train, n_holdout}`) + promoted_to (`staging | shadow | production | null`) + gate_decision (optional auto-promotion-gate tag) + notes + recorded_at. **`InMemoryRetrainingScheduleStore`** refuses duplicate schedules for the same model_id (`duplicate_schedule` → HTTP 409) — operators PATCH the existing one instead of accumulating parallel triggers. Per-tenant cap 50 schedules. `recordSuccess(tenant, model, completed_at, now)` advances `last_retrained_at` + recomputes `next_retrain_at` automatically when a successful outcome lands (only on `status==='success' && completed_at` — failures + in_progress don't shift the schedule). **`InMemoryRetrainingOutcomeStore`** per-tenant cap 500 (FIFO eviction); newest-first sort by `recorded_at`; multi-axis filter (model_id / status / since-ISO). Both stores share the cache-on-init + sync reads + write-through-fire-and-forget pattern from T4.13–T4.18 + T4.6.3. **`buildFleetRetrainingStatus(tenant, schedules, outcomes, now)`** is the rollup: per-model union over schedule + outcome model_ids (sorted asc), per-model `is_overdue` flag (only true when `enabled && next_retrain_at < now` — disabled schedules never go overdue), `ms_until_next` (signed; negative when overdue), `days_since_last_success` (ignores failures — only `status==='success' && completed_at` counts), envelope counters `total_schedules / total_enabled / total_overdue / total_outcomes_30d / total_success_30d / total_failure_30d / success_rate_30d` (rounded 4 decimals; null when no outcomes), `most_recent_outcome` + `all_schedules_current` boolean (= `total_overdue === 0` — the "fleet is healthy" indicator). **7 new BFF routes** (all tenant-gated, all enveloped, all `audit:read` admin-only since retraining is ops-tier control surface): `POST /v1/ai/retraining/schedules` (201 happy / 400 code-routed `EWS_400_<code>` on validation / 409 `EWS_409_duplicate_schedule`); `GET /v1/ai/retraining/schedules` (list); `GET /v1/ai/retraining/schedules/:schedule_id` (200/404); `PATCH /v1/ai/retraining/schedules/:schedule_id` (cadence change auto-recomputes next_retrain_at); `DELETE /v1/ai/retraining/schedules/:schedule_id` (204/404); `POST /v1/ai/retraining/outcomes` (201 — external scheduler posts here; on `status==='success'` the linked schedule advances atomically); `GET /v1/ai/retraining/outcomes?model_id=&status=&since=ISO` (filtered newest-first list); `GET /v1/ai/retraining/status` (fleet rollup). All routes read actor from `X-APEX-USER` header (default 'admin'). 40 new jest tests (8 cadence helpers + 9 ScheduleStore + 6 OutcomeStore + 6 FleetStatus + 11 routes) cover: 5-cadence enum + type guards, computeNextRetrainAt for monthly/quarterly/biannual/annual + drift_triggered null, schedule create+list+update+delete + duplicate-model 409, caller-supplied next_retrain_at preserved, drift_triggered far-future sentinel, invalid cadence/threshold validation, tenant scoping (BIL invisible to BANK_DEMO), recordSuccess auto-advances schedule, outcome record + duration_ms computed, successful outcome auto-advances linked schedule, failure does NOT advance, list filters (model_id / status), non-numeric metrics rejected, invalid promoted_to rejected, fleet empty zero-envelope, overdue flag + all_schedules_current=false, disabled schedule never overdue, success_rate_30d formula, models[] union sort asc with null schedule for ad-hoc + null last_outcome for unrun schedule, days_since_last_success ignores failures, POST schedule happy + 409 duplicate + 400 invalid cadence, GET schedules list + single + 404 + cross-tenant 404, PATCH cadence recompute, DELETE 204→404, POST outcome happy + duration + advances linked schedule, GET outcomes filters, 400 on bad status, GET status fleet rollup, non-admin (risk_analyst lacks audit:read) → 403, tenant scoping through HTTP. Sibling-suite sanity: **146/146 across ai_retraining + ai_auto_promotion_gate + ai_model_promotion + streaming_alert_path** in 2.2s. tsc + node-build clean for T5.1.1 code. **Closes T5.1.** The continuous-learning loop now has every component: drift monitor (T2.6 shipped) → retraining schedule (T5.1.1 this commit) → external trainer (out-of-scope by design — runs in Python/Airflow) → outcome ledger (T5.1.1 this commit) → auto-promotion gate (2026-05-09) → promotion request → registry. The fleet status endpoint composes all of it. **What was deferred (Year-2 Theme E):** actual external scheduler wire-up (Airflow DAG that polls `/v1/ai/retraining/schedules` for due retrains + fires `train_pd.py` + POSTs outcome) — this is operational glue, not contract design. pg-backed `ScheduleStore` + `OutcomeStore` swap will land alongside the auth-svc / cases pg pattern when persistence becomes a demo blocker.

### 2026-05-21 — T2.12.1 — Streaming indicator-event ledger + latency telemetry

- [agent-alert + agent-integration] T2.12.1 shipped — the measurement-layer half of T2.12 ("real-time alert path"). New module `services/bff/src/streaming_alert_path.ts` ships the latency telemetry primitive proving the EWS.docx §3.5 / `docs/slos.md` tier-1 claim of `p95 indicator-observed-at → alert-created-at < 60s`. Three building blocks: (1) **`StreamingIndicatorEventInput` wire shape** — what the producer side POSTs: indicator_id + customer_id + value (finite number) + observed_at (ISO-8601) + optional event_id (deterministic `sie-<tenant>-<ts>-<seq>` when omitted) + optional received_at + optional fired_alert_ids[] + fired_rule_ids[]. (2) **`processStreamingEvent(input, ctx)`** pure function — validates input via guard chain, computes three latency components (`ingest_latency_ms` = received_at − observed_at; `processing_latency_ms` = processed_at − received_at; `total_latency_ms` = processed_at − observed_at), and emits a `StreamingProcessingRecord`. Rejects malformed/missing inputs via `StreamingLedgerError` with codes routed to specific HTTP 400 envelopes: `invalid_input` / `invalid_observed_at` / `invalid_received_at` / `invalid_value` / `observed_in_future` (mapped to `EWS_400_<code>` at the route layer). Defensive: NaN/Infinity values rejected, future observed_at rejected (clock-skew guard), missing tenant_id rejected. (3) **`summarizeStreamingLatency(tenant, records, now)`** analytics aggregator over the ledger — full p50/p95/max/mean/min over `total_latency_ms` + p95 over `processing_latency_ms` separately (split investigation: "is the slow tail us or upstream?"), `count_under_60s` + `count_over_60s` + `percentage_under_60s` (0..1 rounded 4 decimals), **`target_p95_60s_met` boolean** (literal `p95_total_ms < 60_000ms` — the EWS.docx §3.5 budget; vacuously true on empty sample), `by_indicator[]` per-indicator rollup with count + per-id mean/median/p95/max + per-id percentage_under_60s sorted count desc + indicator_id asc tie-break, `total_indicators` distinct count, `most_recent_at` + `oldest_at` recency markers. Re-uses `linearPercentile` from `connector_run_analytics` (the M3.5 / M8.6 / M8.12 family standard) so percentile math stays consistent. **Ledger:** `InMemoryStreamingLedger` with per-tenant cap = 1000 records (oldest evicted on overflow), newest-first `list(tenant, limit?)` reads with default-no-limit, `clear(tenant?)` test helper. `defaultStreamingLedger()` singleton + `_resetDefaultStreamingLedger()` test reset (mirrors the M11.7 / T4.6.3 store pattern). **Constant `STREAMING_SLO_BUDGET_MS = 60_000`** exported for test reuse + future analytics extension. 3 new BFF routes (all tenant-gated, all enveloped, mounted next to M8.6 alert-routing analytics): **POST /v1/streaming/indicator-events** body `{events: [...]}` OR single-event raw shape; RBAC `customers:read_risk_profile` (analyst+ — every operator role can record observations since the rule evaluator can be analyst-driven); 201 with `{tenant_id, recorded_count, events: StreamingProcessingRecord[]}` envelope; 400 with code-routed `EWS_400_<code>` on validation; deterministic seq counter per BFF instance. **GET /v1/streaming/latency?limit=N** — full p50/p95 + by_indicator analytics envelope; RBAC `audit:read` (admin only — latency telemetry is ops-tier observability, gated like the rest of the audit + analytics surface); `?limit` clamped [1, 1000]. **GET /v1/streaming/events?limit=N** — newest-first record list; RBAC `audit:read`; default limit 50. **Scope explicitly bounded:** the upstream Kafka producer wire-up remains Year-2 Theme D — the contract here doesn't depend on the transport (caller supplies observed_at; latency is computed against that clock). The downstream rule-evaluation hook + alert-producer fan-out (T2.12.2 follow-up) wire to existing AlertEvaluator + SmartQueue + AlertRoutingEngine + NotificationBus surfaces (already shipped). This sub-phase owns ONLY the latency telemetry contract — pure pipe enabling measurement of the SLO. **Tests:** 34 new jest tests (9 pure processStreamingEvent + 8 summarizeStreamingLatency + 5 InMemoryStreamingLedger + 12 route): happy path + explicit received_at split + caller event_id preserved + fired_alert_ids round-trip + missing fields rejected + non-finite value rejected + malformed/future observed_at rejected + missing tenant_id rejected (pure); empty input → vacuously-true p95 + null leaderboards / all-fast events 100% under 60s / slow tail breaches budget with p95 ≥ 60s + target_p95_60s_met=false / by_indicator sort canonical / per-indicator percentage_under_60s independent / count_under + count_over = sample_size partition / min ≤ mean ≤ p95 ≤ max ordering (analytics); record + newest-first list / limit respected / cap evicts oldest (5 over cap → first 5 evicted) / tenant scoping (BIL ledger invisible to BANK_DEMO) / clear() empties one tenant (ledger); admin POST happy + bulk envelope + analyst+ accepted + unknown_role 403 (using 'viewer' since field_officer has customers:read_risk_profile) + empty events array 400 + malformed observed_at → EWS_400_invalid_observed_at + future observed_at → EWS_400_observed_in_future / GET /latency admin happy after fast seed shows target met + mixed slow target=false + 403 + cross-tenant invisibility / GET /events newest-first with limit + 403 (routes). 4-suite BFF sibling-sanity check (streaming + alert_routing_analytics + reports_builder_smoke + envelope) — 74/74 pass. tsc + node-build clean for T2.12.1 code. **Closes the measurement half of T2.12.** The remaining indicator→Kafka→rule-evaluator streaming path (T2.12.2) is Year-2 Theme D — the BFF contract here is ready to receive whatever the upstream producer sends.

### 2026-05-20 — T4.6.4 — Self-service reporting: execution engine + run routes + CSV export

- [agent-integration] T4.6.4 shipped — pure `executeReport(def, opts)` at `services/bff/src/reports/builder_execute.ts` is the prototype-phase execution engine. **Flow:** (1) compile via T4.6.2's `compileReportDefinition` (validates source + filter shape + 8 safety rails); (2) synthesise deterministic candidate rows seeded by FNV-1a + Mulberry32 on `(tenant, source, day, definition-hash)` — same input always yields the same rows so SPA tests + demos repeat cleanly; (3) apply filter tree client-side via `evaluateFilter()` recursion (mirrors the SQL compiler's AST walk); (4) aggregate via `applyAggregation()` if group_by + metrics present, with COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX/DISTINCT_COUNT semantics; (5) sort via `applySort()` honouring multi-column ORDER BY; (6) apply LIMIT (already clamped by the compiler); (7) compute grand totals via `computeGrandTotals()` across the resulting groups; (8) return ReportResult envelope. **Synthesis ranges** are catalog-aware: dpd 0-180, bureau_score 300-900, tenure 0-120, count fields 0-50, exposure/balance/outstanding/principal/volume 0-5M KES, pd_score/utilization/criticality 0-1, zscore/drop ±3, dates within last 365 days, datetimes within last 30 days, enums uniform-sampled. PII `name` field synthesises plausible first+last name pairs from a closed list. Per-source CANDIDATE_DEFAULTS sized for realistic distributions: customer_360 2000, loan_360 5000, txn_features 2000, indicator_values 8000, alerts 800, cases 250, approvals 400, audit.event_log 5000. Hard 10000 candidate ceiling for deterministic-fast synthesis. `candidate_target` option overrides for testing. **ReportResult envelope:** tenant_id + generated_at + source_id + is_aggregate + rows + aggregates (cross-row grand totals by metric alias) + total_rows + candidate_rows (pre-filter pool size — surfaces "out of N candidates, M matched") + projection + sql + params + duration_ms. **CSV export** via `reportResultToCsv(result)` — RFC 4180 escaping (quotes around cells with comma/quote/newline; doubled internal quotes; \r\n line breaks; null cells render as empty; non-string values JSON.stringify'd). Trailing \r\n preserved on empty body for stable Content-Length. Production swap to streaming pipe via Node Readable for large result sets is a one-method change without altering the contract. **3 new BFF routes** (mounted right after the T4.6.3 saved-report routes, before M12.1 catalog so /run + /export.csv literals aren't shadowed; all envelope-wrapped except /export.csv which streams text/csv; all `customers:read_risk_profile` analyst+): `POST /v1/reports/builder/run` (ad-hoc definition execution — admin sees compiled sql + params; **non-admin response scrubbed** via `scrubAdminFields()` info-leak guard per docs/risk-register.md R-003 — only admin gets compiled SQL); `POST /v1/reports/builder/saved/:id/run` (tenant + visibility checked via T4.6.3 visibleTo — cross-tenant or not-visible-to-caller returns 404 not 403 to prevent existence-probing); `POST /v1/reports/builder/export.csv` (executes + renders CSV with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="report-<source>-<date>.csv"` for browser download). **Error routing:** ReportExecutionError + FilterCompilerError + ReportCatalogError all → 400 EWS_400_<code>; unknown_source folded to 400 (not 404) on /run since the source_id is in the body not the path. **45 new jest tests (33 pure + 12 route):** **Raw row-list (7):** envelope shape, every row has every projection field, deterministic per (tenant, source, day, def-hash), different tenant→different rows, different day→different rows, different definition→different rows, candidate_target override. **Filter evaluation (7):** eq + gt + between + AND + OR + NOT + in client-side application correctness. **Aggregate (6):** GROUP BY + COUNT, SUM with alias, grand totals across groups (sum-of-groups ≈ envelope.aggregates within $1 rounding), DISTINCT_COUNT, AVG, MIN+MAX with bound invariant. **Sort (2):** DESC monotone-decreasing + ASC monotone-increasing. **Validation (3):** empty tenant_id + unknown source + invalid filter all throw. **CSV (5):** header + body line counts, escapes comma+quote+newline+doubled-quote, null cells empty, numeric cells unquoted, empty rows still emit header. **Routes (15):** /run admin happy + non-admin sql-scrubbed + analyst+ accepted + unknown_role 403 + unknown source 400 + invalid filter 400 + no tenant header 400 + body.tenant_id ignored / /saved/:id/run runs saved def + unknown 404 + cross-tenant 404 / /export.csv returns text/csv + Content-Disposition + projection header + unknown source 400 + unknown_role 403. Full BFF suite: 8473 pass / 58 skipped / 8532 total (pre-existing connector_run_analytics parallel-pool flake passes in isolation). **T4.6 sub-phase status: T4.6.0 + T4.6.1 + T4.6.2 + T4.6.3 + T4.6.4 closed; T4.6.5 SPA page scaffold next.** **Capabilities delivered:** execution engine with deterministic synthesis + filter evaluation + aggregation + sort + CSV streaming + admin-only SQL surfacing. **Capabilities remaining:** SPA report-builder page + saved-list + filter-tree UI (T4.6.5) / SPA section configurator + drill-down + PDF/Excel export (T4.6.6) / Postman + integration smoke + nav (T4.6.7).

### 2026-05-20 — T4.6.2 — Self-service reporting: filter compiler + preview route

- [agent-integration] T4.6.2 shipped — pure `compileReportDefinition(def, {tenant_id})` at `services/bff/src/reports/builder_filter.ts` walks a FilterNode AST and emits a parameterised SQL WHERE clause + complete SELECT against the T4.6.1 catalog. **FilterNode discriminated union:** logical (AND/OR with children[] + NOT with child) + 11 leaf ops (eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge/in/not_in/between/is_null/is_not_null). **ReportDefinition shape:** source_id + filters + group_by + metrics + sort + limit + sections (sections opaque to compiler — consumed by T4.6.5 SPA configurator). **ReportMetric:** field + agg (closed-enum 6 values COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX/DISTINCT_COUNT) + optional alias. **8 safety rails (the contract from T4.6.0 §3.3):** (1) field whitelist via `getReportField` lookup against T4.6.1 catalog — unknown_field throws; (2) per-field type-check via `validateValue` — string/integer/number/boolean/date(YYYY-MM-DD regex)/datetime(ISO regex)/enum each with type-specific guard, type-mismatch throws `invalid_value`; (3) enum-check — `eq`/`ne`/`in`/`not_in` on enum field rejects out-of-enum values with `enum_violation` code; (4) parameterise via `:p0`, `:p1`, ... ParamBag — no string-concat anywhere; (5) `assertSafeSql` rejects 10 forbidden patterns (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE/GRANT/REVOKE/CREATE + multi-statement `;\s*\w` guard) — reused from T2.9 NL→SQL; (6) auto-inject `tenant_id = :tenant_id` predicate for tenant_scoped sources (every catalog source per T4.24 P3) — caller body.tenant_id ignored, JWT/header context wins; (7) hard LIMIT clamped to `[1, MAX_LIMIT=10000]` default 100 + param `:limit`; (8) SELECT-only — generated SQL never DDL/DML. **Type-comparison invariants:** `<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=` only valid on `COMPARABLE_TYPES` (integer/number/date/datetime); strings + enums + booleans only support eq/ne/in/not_in; between requires comparable type. **Aggregate semantics:** group_by + metrics required together for is_aggregate=true; SUM/AVG require NUMERIC + aggregatable flag; MIN/MAX valid on comparable + enum + string; COUNT/DISTINCT_COUNT valid on any field; sort field MUST be in projection (group_by + metric aliases) for aggregate reports OR in source fields for raw row lists. **Complexity caps:** MAX_PARAMS=200 hard cap on filter complexity; AND/OR ≤ 20 children; in/not_in ≤ 100 array elements; between requires exactly 2-element array. **CompiledQuery result envelope:** sql + params + source + projection + param_count + is_aggregate (the SPA renders projection columns + uses params for client-side display). New BFF route `POST /v1/reports/builder/preview` (analyst+, mounted with the other /builder/* routes BEFORE M12.1 /catalog so /preview literal isn't shadowed; envelope-wrapped both directions; tenant always from JWT/header — body.tenant_id ignored; FilterCompilerError → 400 with code-specific `EWS_400_<code>` envelope; unknown_source → 404 `EWS_404_unknown_source`; ReportCatalogError + FilterCompilerError distinguished by `e.name` discriminator). **53 new jest tests (47 pure + 6 route):** basic compile (raw row-list / tenant_id auto-inject / LIMIT clamp / missing source_id / unknown source / missing tenant); 9 leaf op tests covering eq + lt + ge + boolean + date + is_null/is_not_null + in + not_in + between with per-type validation; 5 composite tree tests (AND/OR of leaves / nested AND-of-OR + leaf / NOT wraps inner / empty AND throws / > 20 children throws); 9 validation-rejection tests (unknown field / enum violation with correct error code / type-mismatch with correct code / non-integer into integer / null in comparison / empty in array / non-array between / between on enum / < on string); 6 aggregate tests (group_by + COUNT / SUM with alias / DISTINCT_COUNT / SUM on non-numeric throws / aggregate-without-metrics throws / group_by on non-groupable name field throws); 4 sort tests (DESC / multi-column / metric alias / unknown field throws / invalid direction throws); 5 safety invariants (SELECT-prefix / tenant_id always present / LIMIT always present / params record contains tenant_id+limit / no DDL/DML in compiled SQL); 6 route tests (admin happy + sql/params/projection/is_aggregate in response / analyst+ accepted / unknown_role 403 / unknown source 404 / enum violation routed to 400 with EWS_400_enum_violation / body.tenant_id ignored + JWT wins). Full BFF suite: ~8286 pass / 58 skipped / 8344 total (pre-existing parallel-pool flakes pass in isolation). **T4.6 sub-phase status: T4.6.0 + T4.6.1 + T4.6.2 closed; T4.6.3 saved-report CRUD store + pg migration + reports:share RBAC scope next.** **Capabilities delivered:** filter tree AST compile to parameterised SQL with 8 safety rails + role-bounded preview route. **Capabilities remaining:** saved-report CRUD (T4.6.3) / execution engine (T4.6.4) / SPA builder (T4.6.5-6) / Postman + smoke (T4.6.7).

### 2026-05-20 — T2.9 — NL→SQL Copilot stub

- [agent-ai] T2.9 shipped — pure `translateNlToSql({question, tenant_id, limit?})` at `services/bff/src/copilot/nl_to_sql.ts` is the stub-mode pattern-match resolver translating natural-language analytics questions into safe parameterised SELECTs against the `mart.*` schema. 10 canonical intents in closed enum `NL_TO_SQL_INTENTS`: high_risk_customers (PD-sorted risk-level=High lookup against customer_360) / alerts_by_severity (GROUP BY severity over indicator_values where breach_severity IS NOT NULL) / avg_dpd_by_product (AVG(worst_dpd) GROUP BY product_code over loan_360) / top_npa_customers (JOIN customer_360+loan_360 on has_npa=true ORDER BY outstanding_balance DESC) / indicator_value_lookup (regex-extracted indicator_id e.g. FIN-001 with uppercase normalisation) / customer_count_by_segment (GROUP BY risk_level) / loan_portfolio_summary (per-product count + total outstanding + NPA-only outstanding) / utilization_above_threshold (decimal 0.85 OR percentage 85% form regex-extracted; clamped to [0,1]) / txn_volume_trend (z-score abs-magnitude sort over txn_features) / alert_count_last_n_days (extracted N; clamped [1, 365] with NOW() − N::interval). Each catalog entry: patterns[] (regex array, first match wins) + resolve(matches, tenant, limit) → {sql, params, explanation} builder + confidence score 0.80-0.92 per intent. **Safety rails (5 layers):** (1) Forbidden-keyword regexes (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/ALTER/TRUNCATE/GRANT/REVOKE/CREATE + multi-statement `;\\s*\\w` guard) checked via `assertSafeSql` — any match throws `NlToSqlError('unsafe_query')` mapped to 500 EWS_500_unsafe_query. (2) mart.* schema only — no raw.* or app_*.* cross-reads (asserted by test). (3) Tenant-scoped via `tenant_id = :tenant_id` parameter (NEVER string-concat, asserted by every-SQL test). (4) Hard LIMIT injected with caller-configurable limit clamped to [1, MAX_LIMIT=1000] default 100. (5) `requires_review: true` always TRUE in stub mode (operator MUST eyeball before run — production may drop this once LLM confidence is calibrated). Unmatched question → fallback `intent: 'unknown'` + `fallback: true` + `confidence: 0` + SQL comment block listing 4 available mart tables + 7 example prompts. Validation rejects non-object input / empty or whitespace question / question > 1000 chars / missing tenant_id / non-integer limit — all via `NlToSqlError('invalid_input')` → 400 EWS_400_invalid_input. **Production swap** = Claude API `messages.create` call (Anthropic SDK already wired in `services/bff/src/copilot/llm.ts` for the /v1/copilot/chat path; one-line replacement satisfying the same `NlToSqlResult` shape; activates when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` env var present; preserves all 5 safety rails post-LLM via `assertSafeSql` on returned SQL). New route `POST /v1/copilot/nl-to-sql` (audit:read admin-only — power feature; analysts shouldn't issue arbitrary SQL; envelope-wrapped both request + response; mounted before `/v1/copilot/chat`; header-injected tenant ALWAYS wins so caller cannot override via body.tenant_id). 37 jest tests (26 pure + 11 route) cover all 10 intents matched correctly with SQL + params + confidence + explanation; indicator-id regex extraction with hyphen variant + uppercase normalisation; utilization decimal (0.85) vs percentage (85%) form + clamp to [0,1]; alert-count days extraction + clamp [1, 365]; fallback path returns intent=unknown + fallback=true + confidence=0 + comment + available tables; validation rejection paths (non-object, empty, whitespace-only, 1001-char, missing tenant_id, non-integer limit); limit clamping (default 100 / clamp to MAX_LIMIT=1000 / clamp to min=1); safety invariants (every generated SQL starts with SELECT or WITH, queries only mart.* schema not raw.* or app_*, every SQL tenant-scoped via parameter, requires_review always TRUE, intent enum is closed); admin route happy + 403 non-admin + 400 missing question + 400 overlong question + tenant header injection cannot be overridden by body.tenant_id + limit param honoured and clamped + unmatched returns 200 with fallback + 400 no tenant header. ### 2026-05-20 — X.3 — IaC + container scan in CI

- [agent-integration] X.3 shipped — `.github/workflows/security-scan.yml` adds a 3-job CI workflow on push-to-main + every PR touching `infra/terraform/**` / `services/**` / `web/**`. **Job 1 `iac-scan`:** Trivy IaC mode (config scan) on `infra/terraform` covering AWS misconfigurations + CIS benchmarks + encryption gaps; Checkov adds policy-as-code coverage (SOC2/NIST/HIPAA-relevant patterns) over the same Terraform tree. Both produce SARIF uploaded to GitHub Security tab — Trivy with `category: trivy-iac` + Checkov with `category: checkov-iac`. Findings visible per-PR + queryable via the code-scanning API. **Job 2 `container-scan`:** Trivy filesystem scan over a 12-path matrix (10 services + web SPA: services/bff, services/auth-svc, services/audit-svc, services/regulatory-svc/{cases,alerts,rules,indicators}, services/collection-adapter, services/notification-svc, services/pipeline-svc, services/ai-copilot-svc, web) catching transitive npm + python CVEs. Per-matrix SARIF upload with `category: trivy-fs-<path>` so SARIF dedupe doesn't collide across matrix entries. **Job 3 `summary`:** aggregates jobs 1 + 2 for branch-protection rules — pin required-status-check on the single name `security-scan / summary`. **Critical-only gate semantics** per `docs/pentest-remediation-playbook.md` §1 SLA matrix: CI fails on any CRITICAL severity finding (Critical has 3-day patch SLA + war-room — merging NEW Critical findings would breach that contract); HIGH severity warns via SARIF but doesn't block (14-day patch SLA → not a merge blocker per remediation policy); MEDIUM + below visible-only via SARIF dashboard. Implementation: each scan uses `exit-code: '0'` so Trivy doesn't fail itself, then follow-up `jq` step counts `results[].level == 'error'` (SARIF maps Critical → error) and fails CI if > 0. `ignore-unfixed: true` on filesystem scan reduces noise (already covered by `docs/bau-runbook.md` §5 annual vendor security review per X.1). Permissions block: `security-events: write` for SARIF upload + `contents: read` for checkout. Companion to existing CI gates (`schema-compat.yml` for T3.8 Kafka BACKWARD compat + `services-ci.yml` for jest+tsc+vitest across 12 workspaces + `terraform-ci.yml` for fmt+validate+5-layer matrix + `rbac-matrix.yml` for T3.9 matrix consistency) — all 5 workflows now form the full security + correctness gate per `docs/charter.md` §3 success criteria + `docs/risk-register.md` R-003 (tenant isolation bypass — RBAC tests) + R-014 (RBAC matrix drift — CI gate) mitigations. **Cross-cutting status: X.1 + X.2 + X.3 closed; X.4 adoption metrics still to ship.**

### 2026-05-14 — T6 M14.21 — Field visit geo-clustering

- [agent-integration] M14.21 shipped — pure `clusterFieldVisits(visits, radius_km)` at `services/bff/src/field_visit_geo_clustering.ts` does greedy Haversine clustering of M14.10 field visits with GPS pins. Visits without `location` are counted in `total_without_gps` but skipped from clustering. Greedy O(n × k) algorithm: walk visits oldest-first, assign each to the FIRST existing cluster whose centroid is within `radius_km`; if none, start a new cluster. Running-mean centroid (`c' = c + (point - c) / (n+1)`). Per-cluster shape `{cluster_id, centroid: {lat, lon}, visit_count, officer_ids[] (sorted asc), customer_ids[] (sorted asc), by_outcome (all 6 keys), latest_visit_at}`. Clusters sorted by visit_count desc → latest_visit_at desc. Default radius 1 km, max 500 km (silently clamped); non-positive radius falls back to default. Haversine helper exported separately for testability (verified Mumbai-Delhi ≈ 1148 km, equatorial 1° ≈ 111 km, antipodal ≈ 20015 km). New route `GET /v1/field/visits/geo-clusters?radius_km=N&since=ISO` (`audit:read`). 19 new jest tests (4 haversine + 5 unit covering empty + no-GPS skip + within-radius cluster + outside-radius separate + centroid running mean + latest_visit_at + sort order + 3 radius tuning + 7 route assertions). ### 2026-05-07 — Real-backend dev mode wired end-to-end (3 commits)

Spent the session moving the SPA off MSW and onto the live BFF + auth-svc + Postgres so a `make up`-style developer flow renders real data on every page, not just the offline mocks.

- **SPA dev wiring** — `vite.config.ts` proxy forwards `/api/*` → BFF (`:8084`), `/v1/*` → BFF, `/auth/*` → auth-svc (`:8080`); `web/.env.development.local` toggle (`VITE_USE_MSW=false`) flips MSW off. Default still on so the offline demo path (`make web-dev` no env file) keeps working.
- **`web/src/lib/http.ts`** — request interceptor auto-injects `X-Tenant-ID` (from auth store, default `BANK_DEMO`) + `X-Channel: API` + `X-Source-System: apex-ews-spa` so every `/v1` call passes the bank-grade envelope gate. Response interceptor auto-unwraps `{header, body}` so callers see the body directly.
- **Type cleanup** — `EnvelopeBody<T>` aliased to `T` (transparent); 14 stale `r.data.body` accessors stripped across `lib/api.ts`, `cms/api.ts`, `rules/EwsRuleBuilderPage.tsx`, `rules/EwsRuleWizardPage.tsx`, `rules/rulesPlusApi.ts`. `tsc --noEmit` clean across the SPA.
- **Page hardening** — `DashboardPage.tsx` non-null assertions (`data!.x.toLocaleString()`) replaced with `data ? data.x.toLocaleString() : '—'` so a slow / 401 / cold cache renders placeholders instead of crashing.
- **5 new BFF `/api/*` facades** — `/api/dashboard/summary`, `/api/customers`, `/api/customers/:id/risk`, `/api/rules`, `/api/cases` (+ `/api/cases/:id`). Each is a SPA-internal flavor that doesn't require the full envelope/tenant context — they aggregate from the BFF in-memory stores or proxy to cases-svc.
- **Criticality computed server-side** — `services/bff/src/mapping.ts` now populates `criticality_score`, `confidence`, `customer_exposure_kes`, `linked_alert_ids` on every `AlertRow` (formula mirrors `web/src/lib/criticality.ts`). Honours `?dedup=true&sort=criticality` query params. `CustomerLookup.exposure_kes` added so per-customer exposure feeds the score.
- **Extended seeds** — 14 new customers (c-107..c-120, with realistic exposures), 5 new rules (r-30..r-34) including 2 V2 maker-checker entries (`Cross-product default cascade`, `Direct-debit bounce ≥ 3 in 30d`), 13 alerts seeded into `services/regulatory-svc/alerts/.outbox/` so the SPA queue ranks Olivia Cherop (8.45) → Faisal Hussein (8.16) → Achieng Otieno (7.7).
- **Cold-start seeders for in-memory stores** — `seedDemoCmsCases()` adds 8 demo CMS investigations into `defaultCmsCaseStore` on bootstrap; existing `seedDefaultEwsRules()` invoked for both `BANK_DEMO` and `BIL` so `/v1/ews/rules` ships 10 brief-mandated rules per tenant.
- **Postgres bring-up** — `apex-ews-pg` (postgres:16, port 55432, db apex_ews, role apex/apex). Migrations 001-015 applied (skipping 010_mart_tenant.sql which depends on `mart.customer_360` from `dbt run`). `_generate_app_seeds.py` produces 26,169 rows across 12 tables (505 users, 528 cases, 2527 alerts, 120 saved scenarios, 25 webhook subs + 915 deliveries, 12k audit events). With `CASES_PG_URL` / `ALERTS_PG_URL` / `BFF_PG_URL` set, the cases-svc, alerts-svc, and BFF (scenarios + webhooks) read/write Postgres instead of in-memory.

  - `data/dbt/dbt_project.yml` + missing `data/dbt/macros/generate_schema_name.sql` — default schema-resolution prefixed `<target>_<custom>`, so seeds landed in `staging_raw` instead of `raw`. Added a `generate_schema_name` macro that returns the literal custom schema. Also dropped the orphaned `staging_raw` schema.
  - `data/dbt/models/staging/schema.yml` — three `accepted_values` tests had `quote: false`, which made dbt render string values as bare SQL identifiers (`column "male" does not exist`). Removed the `quote: false` override on `stg_customer.gender`, `stg_customer.kyc_status`, `stg_bureau_score.score_band`.
  - `ml/data/load_from_mart.py` — the SCHEMA_QUERY referenced columns the dbt mart doesn't materialise (`utilization`, `dpd_max_90d`, `balance_drop_30d_pct`, `defaulted_within_60d`, `snapshot_date`). Rewrote the query to project the actual mart columns into the contracted feature names: `worst_dpd → dpd_max_90d`, `exposure_to_income_ratio → utilization`, `arrears_repayment_count → repayment_delay_streak`, derived `tenure_months` from `onboarded_at`, derived `txn_volume_zscore_90d` over the population from `txn_features`, mapped `loan_360.product_code` (PL_RET/AUTO_RET/INV_SME/WC_SME/CORP_TL) to PRODUCT_LEVELS, banded `monthly_income` to INCOME_LEVELS, mapped `has_npa::int → defaulted_within_60d`. Also fixed the `WHERE c.as_of BETWEEN ...` bound — `as_of` is a `timestamptz`, casting to `::date` for the date-range compare.
  - `ml/pipelines/train_pd.py` — XGB hyperparameters (`min_child_weight=5`, `n_estimators=500`) were tuned for the 4 000-row synthetic dataset; on the 176-row mart slice with 8 positives no leaf can satisfy `mcw=5` so the tree never splits and the model collapses to a constant predictor (AUC 0.5). Added an auto-switch: when `n_positives < 20` the trainer downshifts to `mcw=1, n_estimators=300, max_depth=4`, uses sigmoid (Platt) calibration in place of isotonic, and clamps the K-fold CV to `min(KFOLDS, n_positives)`. The synthetic-tuned defaults are preserved for the 4 000-row path.
  - Installed `sqlalchemy>=2.0` + `psycopg2-binary` into the venv (the loader's `from sqlalchemy import …` was unsatisfied).
- [orchestrator] B2 — `python ml/data/load_from_mart.py --start 2026-04-27 --end 2026-04-27` then `python ml/pipelines/train_pd.py`. Mart-trained challenger v0.1.0 metrics: AUC 1.0, KS 1.0, Brier 0.0023, CV-AUC 1.0±0.0 on n_train=176 / n_holdout=44 (8 + 4 positives). **Caveat:** AUC=1.0 is a leakage artifact — `mart.customer_360.has_npa` is defined in dbt as `npa_status IN ('SUBSTANDARD','DOUBTFUL','LOSS')`, which the simulator data assigns directly off `days_past_due`, i.e. the same signal as the `dpd_max_90d` feature. The synthetic-trained 0.8822 model stays champion. To get an honest mart-split AUC we'd need either (a) a `has_npa` definition not co-linear with the DPD feature or (b) a much larger seed (current `N_CUSTOMERS=220` gives only 12 positives total).

Schema-only — service-wiring (services actually reading/writing the new tables instead of in-memory stores) is deferred per Gap 3 part B in [`docs/database-gap-analysis.md`](docs/database-gap-analysis.md). Two new docs published in this session: [`docs/database-schema.md`](docs/database-schema.md) (column-level reference for all 9 schemas) and [`docs/database-gap-analysis.md`](docs/database-gap-analysis.md) (live inventory + sized fix plans).

**1. Scaled raw seed 45×** — `data/dbt/seeds/_generate_seeds.py` knobs bumped from `N_CUSTOMERS=220 / N_LOANS_TARGET=520 / N_TXNS_TARGET=6000` to `10_000 / 24_000 / 280_000`; safety cap on repayments removed (no longer needed). Re-ran `dbt seed --full-refresh` (3m52s) + `dbt run` (7s) + `dbt test` (1.3s). All 79 dbt tests still pass on the larger volume. New raw row counts: 10,000 customers / 24,000 loans / 247,550 repayments / 289,819 transactions / 10,000 bureau scores. Mart rebuilds: `mart.customer_360` 10k / `mart.loan_360` 24k / `mart.txn_features` 10k / `mart.indicator_values` 80k. NPA ratio: 4.25% (1,019 of 24,000 loans), 528 unique defaulted customers.

**2. Closed Gap 1** — the 5 `raw.cbs_*` tables defined in `002_raw_tables.sql` had sat empty for the entire prototype lifecycle. Schema lied: anyone reading the SQL thought a CBS loader wrote to those tables, but data actually lived in `raw.seed_*` (loaded by dbt seed) and the `sources.yml` aliases hid the redirect. Fixed cleanly:
  - Dropped the 5 empty tables: `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS raw.cbs_customer_profile;` and 4 siblings.
  - Rewrote [`002_raw_tables.sql`](data/schema/002_raw_tables.sql) — declares only the `seed_*` tables that actually carry data; original `cbs_*` schemas preserved in git history for reinstatement when T1.4b ships the real CBS loader.
  - Cleaned [`data/dbt/models/sources.yml`](data/dbt/models/sources.yml) — dropped all 5 `identifier:` aliases; sources reference `seed_*` directly.
  - Mechanical rename across the 5 staging models (`{{ source('raw', 'seed_customers') }}` etc.).

**3. Added 5 new application schemas** via [`data/schema/004_app_schemas.sql`](data/schema/004_app_schemas.sql) — gives the operational stores a real Postgres home. Production target wiring is the next sessions' work.
  - `app_iam.{users, sessions, password_history, audit_events}` — owned by `services/auth-svc`. CHECK constraints on role + event_type. FKs sessions/password_history → users with CASCADE.
  - `app_cases.{cases, actions}` — owned by `services/regulatory-svc/cases`. CHECK on state ∈ {open, assigned, in_action, monitored, closed} + outcome ∈ {cured, cured_temp, defaulted}; partial index on sla_status for {approaching, breached}.
  - `app_alerts.{alerts, queue_assignments}` — owned by `services/regulatory-svc/alerts`. Carries the criticality_score + customer_exposure_kes fields added in the 2026-05-02 prioritization work.
  - `app_bff.{webhook_subscriptions, webhook_deliveries}` — owned by `services/bff` webhooks. Secret column is hex HMAC key; never returned via list/get APIs.
  - `app_scenario.saved_scenarios` — JSONB result column preserves the full ScenarioResult so reload shows saved numbers (not a re-run if engine elasticities change).

**4. Generated synthetic app data** via [`data/schema/_generate_app_seeds.py`](data/schema/_generate_app_seeds.py) (seed=43, deterministic). Produces `app_seeds.sql` (~26,000 rows) loaded via `psql -f`:
  - `app_iam.users`: 505 (5 demo accounts u-001..u-005 verbatim from `services/auth-svc/src/users.ts` + 500 synthetic)
  - `app_iam.sessions`: 3,105 (avg ~6 per user, ~35% revoked, mix of Chrome/Firefox/Mobile/Safari)
  - `app_iam.password_history`: 1,445 (avg 2-3 historical hashes per user)
  - `app_iam.audit_events`: 12,000 (14 event types weighted by realistic frequency)
  - `app_cases.cases`: 528 (one per defaulted customer; mix of all 5 states; SLA distribution)
  - `app_cases.actions`: 1,568 (avg ~3 actions per non-open case; GPS for visit actions)
  - `app_alerts.alerts`: 2,527 (defaulted cohort + 50% of WATCH-status loan customers; criticality_score computed via the production formula)
  - `app_alerts.queue_assignments`: 3,431 (avg ~1.4 assignments per alert showing reassignment history)
  - `app_bff.webhook_subscriptions`: 25 (22 active, 3 deactivated; realistic names like "AML Hub primary", "PagerDuty critical", "Slack #risk-alerts")
  - `app_bff.webhook_deliveries`: 915 (~92% success rate; failures show 500/502/503/0/401)
  - `app_scenario.saved_scenarios`: 120 (12 named templates × ~10 quarter-tagged variants)

**5. Final state in DBeaver:** **9 schemas / 21 tables / ~731,500 rows.** The dev container at `apex-ews-pg:55432` shows everything alive. Connect with role `apex` / db `apex_ews`.
